title: Why cover the cusps? Cusp flexure after RCT
topic: Losing the marginal ridges, not the endo access, is what lets cusps flex; covering the cusps splints them.

claims.claim: Intact tooth: marginal ridges brace the cusps (100% stiffness reference)
claims.source: Reeh ES, Messer HH, Douglas WH. J Endod 1989;15(11):512-6 (PMID 2639947)

claims.claim: Test load F = 111 N (37 N/s for 3 s), maxillary premolars, cervical strain gauges, in vitro
claims.source: Reeh ES, Messer HH, Douglas WH. J Endod 1989;15(11):512-6 (PMID 2639947); 111 N derived from 37 N/s × 3 s

claims.claim: Endo access + RCT with ridges intact: only −5% stiffness (bar B 95%)
claims.source: Reeh ES, Messer HH, Douglas WH. J Endod 1989;15(11):512-6 (PMID 2639947)

claims.claim: MOD cavity, both marginal ridges cut: −63% stiffness (bar C 37%)
claims.source: Reeh ES, Messer HH, Douglas WH. J Endod 1989;15(11):512-6 (PMID 2639947)

claims.claim: Cusps splay more as stiffness falls; delta drawn proportional to 1/stiffness, exaggerated
claims.source: Toy model / schematic: deflection not to scale; direction supported by Panitvisai P, Messer HH. J Endod 1995;21(2):57-61 (PMID 7714437)

claims.claim: Cuspal-coverage cast-gold onlay: stiffness restored, 211% of intact (separate in-vitro series)
claims.source: Reeh ES, Douglas WH, Messer HH. J Dent Res 1989;68(11):1540-4 (PMID 2584522)

claims.claim: Onlay splints the cusps (full occlusal coverage strengthens all cusps)
claims.source: Linn J, Messer HH. J Endod 1994;20(10):479-85 (PMID 7714419); in vitro, 36 mandibular molars, gold/amalgam overlays

claims.claim: 6× tooth-loss rate when not crowned after RCT (adjusted HR 6.0, 95% CI 3.2-11.3; 203 teeth; retrospective, any cause, association only)
claims.source: Aquilino SA, Caplan DJ. J Prosthet Dent 2002;87(3):256-63 (PMID 11941351)

claims.claim: Posterior endo tooth with a ridge lost: cover the cusps (onlay or crown)
claims.source: Mannocci F et al. ESE position statement. Int Endod J 2021;54(11):1974-81 (PMID 34378217)

caption:
Why cover the cusps after RCT? Blame the marginal ridges, not the access.

In vitro (maxillary premolars): access + RCT in an otherwise intact tooth cut cusp stiffness by only ~5%. An MOD prep cut it by ~63%.
A cast-gold onlay took stiffness above intact (2.11×, separate series).
Clinically, teeth not crowned after RCT were lost at 6× the rate (retrospective, association only).
Posterior tooth, ridge lost? Cover the cusps: onlay or crown.

Refs: Reeh 1989 (J Endod; J Dent Res) · Linn & Messer 1994 (J Endod) · Aquilino 2002 (J Prosthet Dent) · ESE position statement (Int Endod J 2021)
